direction.semantic: reading direction consumed by Base UI components for behavior (keyboard, positioning, slider direction)

children.semantic: wrap the app or a subtree

renderProp: Not applicable — context provider, renders no element. Additional export: `useDirection()` returns the current TextDirection, which is the recommended way to read direction inside portaled content that escapes a `dir` attribute set deeper in the tree.
controlled: Not applicable — `direction` is a simple value prop (no default/open state, no callbacks).
notableDifferences: React Aria uses <I18nProvider locale> plus `dir`; Base UI splits the concern: <DirectionProvider direction> only changes component BEHAVIOR. You must still set dir='rtl' (or direction: rtl CSS) in your own code — the docs state this explicitly.

Exact export surface (verified in direction-provider/index.d.ts): `export { Provider as DirectionProvider, useDirection, type TextDirection } from './index.parts.js'` — the namespace alias inside index.parts is `Provider`, but the public name is DirectionProvider.
No locale/i18n concerns (no number, date or message formatting) — direction only.
